2.  The present second bail has been filed on behalf of the applicant in R.C. No. 120 2022 A 0008,
under Section - 120-B read with Sections - 409, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C. and Section - 7 and 13(2)

420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C. and Section - 7 and 13 (2) r/w 13 (1) (a) of P.C. Act and Section - 66 of I.T.

Muzaffarnagar regarding fraud in refund of Rs.1,39,31,370/- by the officials of the Income Tax Department, Muzaffar Nagar Range Office and private persons

. It was alleged that Saurabh Singh,
the then TA now Sr. T.A. and Abhay Singh, the then Sr. T.A. now OS, worked out several refunds unauthorisedly and by using token of the Income Tax Officer (ITO) and the same were forwarded to the Range for approval.

The refund approval requests were moved on the systems by these officials of Ward/Circle and then approved on the system from Range Office fraudulently by using the RSA token of the supervisory officer.

In that process, Abhay Kant, the then Sr. TA, Saurabh Singh, the then TA, now Sr. TA and Rohit Kumar (applicant), the then Stenographer (now Inspector of Income Tax), were involved in fraudulent issuance of refund pertaining to eleven assesses.

It was found that Abhay Kant, Saurabh Singh, applicant- Rohit Kumar, Gopal Yadav the then Sr. TA and Sanjay Agarwal (ITO) misused the RSA tokens of the (AOs) to work out and authenticate generation of fictitious refunds payable to assesses on the System and got the refunds credited to the bank accounts of assesses, disclosed in their ITR.
The TDS credit claimed in ITRs were increased by them fictitiously and refund worked out on old system application of AST.

Total 11 assesses of Khatauli Ward were issued refunds between 18.08.2020 to 26.08.2021 and thereby fictitious refund of Rs.
1,39,31,370/- was made.

During investigation, it was found that for issuing fraudulent rectifications,
Abhay Kant STA received an amount of Rs. 2.45 lakhs which was credited in his account through account of assessee Siraj Malik and applicant Rohit Kumar.
Fraudulent tax refund in respect of assessees Noor Mohammad and Abid Hussain was purportedly done by Saurabh Singh by using computers having distinctive I.P. addresses allotted to them.
For issuing fraudulent rectifications Saurabh Singh has received an illegal gratification of Rs. 20,000/- credited in his account through account of applicant Rohit Kumar.

Fraudulent tax refund in respect of assessee Yameen, Faimuddin,
Abid Hussain and Abdul Qulam purportedly was done by applicant Rohit Kumar and Abhay Kant by using distinctive I.P. addresses allotted to them.

For issuing fraudulent rectifications, applicant Rohit Kumar received an amount of Rs. 4 lakh in his account as pecuniary benefits from the assessee/accused Siraj Malik vide two cheques of Rs. 2 lakhs through one Rohit Kumar (private person).

It was found that refunds have been worked out by increasing the claim of T.D.S. of the assessees, which exceeded TDS claim in return, by passing rectification under Section - 154 Income Tax Act at the level of ITO/DCIT on their system without having any application from the assessees.
4. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
During inquiry, co-accused Abhay Kant and Saurabh Singh have admitted in writing regarding involvement in fraudulent processing of refund orders.
Applicant has also filed an application during departmental inquiry.
Referring to facts of the matter, it was submitted that there is no credible evidence against applicant.

Further, only Assessing Officers were assigned the job of processing and working out of claim of refund of an assessee, whereas applicant was discharging his duty as Income Tax Inspector and thus he could not have played any role in processing and working out of the refund claims of the assessees.
The RSA token is totally tamper proof and it can be used only by the authorised person.
Income Tax Inspector or stenographer is not included in the list of officials entitled for use of RSA token.

Only Assessing Officer can allow a refund by passing a specific order and that too by using his own RSA token and in case amount of refund exceeds Rs. one lakh, refund can be made only after approval of Joint Commissioner.
In the instant matter, the refund in question was more than Rs. one lakh and as such it could not have been made without specific order by Assessing Officer and approval by the Joint Commissioner.

sentences.text: There is no such version of prosecution that Pankaj Kumar Sharma, Sanjay Agarwal, Alok Nath and Mayank Kumar have authorised applicant to use their RSA token.

All the computers installed in Ward and in Range of Income Tax office are interconnected through internet/intranet and thus whatever work is done on the system, the data is saved on the main server and higher officials can easily see whatever work has been done by any of the official.

5. It is further submitted that as per prosecution version, in processing refunds of six assessees,
computer allotted to applicant was used but no inference can be drawn for his involvement in processing and working out fifteen refunds of six assessees.
The attending facts show that co-accused Abhay Kant may have been instrumental in processing and working out refunds.

It was submitted that from 20.01.2021 to 01.06.2021 applicant was posted as stenographer in Income Tax Office Khatauli, whereas claim of department is that from 2019 till his retirement in January, 2022 co-accused Gopal Yadav was working as Senior Tax Inspector and that Gopal Yadav has passed user ID and RSA token to Abhay Kant and Rohit Kumar.
The facts of the matter indicate that Gopal Yadav has shared the confidential details of User ID and RSA token of Alok Nath to Abhay Kant.
During departmental inquiry, co-accused Abhay Kant and Saurabh Singh have already admitted their involvement.
Transfer of PAN of assessees from Khatauli Ward (3)(2)(5) to Khatauli Ward 3(2)(4) and Circle 3(1)(1) does not link the applicant in any manner.

6. Further, as per prosecution version, applicant received Rs.2 lakhs in his account on transfer from account of Rohit Kumar (private person) and Rs.2 lakhs from account of Kusum Devi and allegedly co-accused Siraj Malik had deposited these amounts in their accounts and thus, said Rohit Kumar and Kusum Devi were hand in glove with Siraj Malik but they have not been made accused.

It was submitted that Rohit Kumar and Kusum Devi have transferred Rs.3,80,000/- in account of applicant and the matter of deposition of any amount by co-accused Siraj Malik in the account of Rohit Kumar and Kusum Devi was purely a private transaction and it has no concern with applicant.
Statements of Rohit Kumar (private person) and Kusum Devi are not admissible in evidence against applicant.
There is no such specific allegation that any entrustment of public money was made with applicant or he has misappropriated the same and thus no offence under Section - 409 I.P.C. is made out.

Similarly, there is no material to make out a case under Section - 465, 467, 471 I.P.C.
against the applicant.
Several assessees have been granted bail by the trial court and case of the applicant is on better footing than them.

7. It is further submitted that applicant was not arrested by the investigating officer during investigation and now charge-sheet has already been filed and thus in view of dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs Central Bureau of Investigation and Another,
reported in (2021) 10 SCC 773, applicant-accused is entitled for bail.

8. Sri Sanjay Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for C.B.I. has opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that Abhay Kant, Saurabh Singh and applicant Rohit Kumar while officiating in different tenures Rohit Kumar vs Cbi on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198336306/

The refund approval requests were moved on the systems by these officials of Ward/Circle and then approved on system from Range office fraudulently by using RSA token of supervisory officer.

It was submitted that Abhay Kant, the then Sr. TA, Saurabh Singh, the then Tax Assistant and applicant Rohit Kumar, the then Steno (now Inspector) were involved in the fraudulent issuance of refunds pertaining to 11 assesses.

Fraudulent tax refunds in respect of assesses Abdul Kalam, Yameen, Noor construction, Mohd. Naim were purportedly done by applicant Rohit Kumar and Abhay Kant by using computers having distinctive I.P. addresses allotted to them.

The detail of fraudulent tax refunds were worked out by applicant Rohit Kumar and Abhay Kant by deceitfully using RSA token and sharing secret six digit number,
which was allotted to Alok Nath ACIT, Sanjay Agarwal ITO and Pankaj Sharma ITO, by hatching a conspiracy.
Accused persons have abused their official position and illegally transferred the PAN Card of assesses from Khatauli Ward 3(2)(5) to Khatauli Ward 3(2)(4) and Circle 3(1)(1).

The accused persons created false rectification orders by using RSA token of Assessing Officers and false rectification orders of assesses were approved unauthorisedly by using RSA tokens of Assessing Officers and transferred the amount in accounts of assesses.
Gopal Yadav, the then Sr. TA provided RSA token of Assessing Officer Alok Nath.

For issuing fraudulent rectifications, applicant Rohit Kumar received an amount of Rs. 4 lakhs in his bank account as pecuniary benefits from the assessee Siraj Malik vide two cheques amounting to Rs. 2 lakhs each routed through account of one Rohit Kumar (private person) and Kusum Devi.

9. It is further submitted that after filing of charge-sheet against the accused persons, summons were issued against them but the applicant / accused did not appear and thus non-bailable warrants were issued against him and applicant was arrested after execution of non-bailable warrants.
It was submitted that in case applicant is granted bail, he may abscond and flee from justice.
Economic offences constitute a class apart and need to be visited with a different approach in matters of bail.
The economic offences having deep routed conspiracies and involving huge loss of public funds need to be viewed seriously.

Learned counsel for C.B.I. has referred case of Neeraj Dutta vs. State (Govt.
Of NCT of Delhi), AIR 2023 SUPREME COURT 330 and A.B. Bhaskara Rao vs. C.B.I., (2011) 10 SCC 259 and submitted that in view of gravity of offence and all attending facts, applicant-accused is not entitled for bail.

sentences.text: I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

11. The instant regular case was registered by the C.B.I. on the complaint of Joint Commissioner of Income Tax, Range-(1), Muzaffarnagar regarding refund fraud of Rs. 1,39,31,370/- committed by the officials of Income Tax Department, Muzaffar Nagar Range Office.

As per prosecution version, it was revealed that Abhay Kant, the then Senior TA, Saurabh Singh, the then Tax Assistant and applicant Rohit Kumar, the then Stenographer (now inspector) while officiating in different tenures worked out certain refunds unauthorisedly while working on system by using token of ITO and the same were pushed to Range for approval.
The refund approval requests were moved on systems by said officials and then approved on the system from Range Office fraudulently by using the RSA token of the supervisory officer.

It was found that applicant Rohit Kumar and aforesaid Abhay Kant and Saurabh Singh were involved in fraudulent issuance of refunds in the tune of Rs.1,39,31,370/-,

4 pertaining to 11 assesses.

sentences.text: As per prosecution version, the processing in respect of assesses Abdul Kalam, Yameen, Noor Constructions and Mohd. Naim was purportedly done by applicant Rohit Kumar and Abhay Kant by using computers having distinctive I.P. addresses allotted to them.

The details of fraudulent tax refunds to the said assesses were worked out by applicant Rohit Kumar and Abhay Kant by deceitfully using RSA token and sharing secret six digit number, which was allotted to Alok Nath ACIT, Sanjay Agarwal ITO and Pankaj Sharma ITO.

They have transferred PAN card of assesses from Khatauli Ward (3)(2)(5) to Khatauli Ward 3(2)(4) and Circle 3(1)(1) and worked out false rectification orders by using RSA token of Assessing Officers and transferred amounts in account of assesses and thereby huge wrongful loss was caused to the Government.

Applicant received an amount of Rs.4 lakhs in his bank account as pecuniary benefit from assessee Siraj Malik vide two cheques amounting to Rs.2 lakhs each routed through bank account of one Rohit Kumar (private person) and Smt, Kusum Devi and this fact is supported by the transactions of bank account of aforesaid persons.

Said Rohit Kumar (private person), who was working in the Income tax office as private assistant, has stated that he was given said two cheques of Rs 2 lacs each issued by Siraj Malik, by the applicant Rohit and he has transferred said amount to applicant through his bank account and through account of his mother Kusum Devi.

The accused persons, including applicant,
have caused a loss of Rs.1,39,31,370/- to the public exchequer by indulging in the aforesaid illegal acts.
Applicant has been shown beneficiary in the tune of Rs. 4 lakhs.

It is correct that during investigation applicant was not arrested by the C.B.I. but it has been shown that after filing of charge-sheet he did not appear before the trial court hence non-bailable warrants were issued against him.
Applicant could be arrested after non-bailable warrants were executed against him.
The instant matter relates economic offence and corruption by public servant and section 409 I.P.C. is punishable up to imprisonment of life
thus, applicant does not deserves bail on the basis of law laid down in case Satender Kumar Antil (supra).
Here, it may be observed that corruption poses a serious threat to our society and it must be dealt with iron hands.
Corruption not only leads to abysmal loss to public exchequer but also tramples good governance.
12. Considering the nature of accusations, complicity of applicant and all attending facts of the matter, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the applicant-accused at this stage.
However, if no significant progress is made in the trial during a period of 7 months from today, the applicant would be at liberty to file a fresh bail application in accordance with law.
13. With the aforesaid observations, the instant bail application is rejected.
